Counsel,

Thank you for the draft. Buyer has reviewed and has the following initial comments.

First, based on Buyer’s preliminary diligence and current market assumptions, the proposed USD 45,000,000 purchase price is not supportable. Buyer proposes a purchase price of USD 36,000,000.

Second, Buyer cannot agree to a 30-day outside closing date from signing. We propose that closing occur within 45 days after satisfaction or waiver of the applicable closing conditions.

Third, the financial-statement representation should not be knowledge-qualified and should be tied to GAAP rather than only the Company’s historically applied accounting principles. Please revise Section 3 to provide that the financial statements fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented, in accordance with GAAP consistently applied, subject only to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes for interim statements.

Finally, Buyer will expect customary protections, including an ordinary-course interim operating covenant, no material adverse effect closing condition, bring-down of representations at closing, and indemnification for breaches of representations and covenants.

Please circulate a revised draft reflecting the above.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Thank you for Buyer’s comments. We have circulated a revised draft reflecting Seller’s movement on the principal business and legal points.

On price, Seller cannot accept USD 36,000,000 in light of the Company’s performance and the value reflected in the materials provided to date. Seller has revised the purchase price to USD 42,000,000 as a constructive counterproposal.

On closing mechanics, we have revised the draft to provide for closing shortly after satisfaction or waiver of the closing conditions, with an outside date to preserve deal certainty. We have also included the customary Buyer protections you identified, subject to customary materiality, consent, survival, basket and cap limitations.

Please let us know if Buyer can work from this draft so we can narrow the remaining issues promptly.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,000,000 for the Shares at Closing, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller.

2. Closing. Subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, Closing shall occur on the third Business Day after satisfaction or waiver of the applicable closing conditions, or on such other date as the parties may agree in writing; provided that, unless otherwise agreed by the parties, Closing shall occur no later than 45 days after signing.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented, in accordance with GAAP consistently applied, subject, in the case of interim financial statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes.

4. Interim Operations. From signing until Closing, except as otherwise contemplated by this Agreement, required by applicable law, or consented to by the Buyer, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, the Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course of business in all material respects and shall not take any action outside the ordinary course that would reasonably be expected to be materially adverse to the Company.

5. Conditions to Closing. The Buyer’s obligation to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to: (a) the representations and warranties of the Seller being true and correct at Closing, except where the failure to be true and correct would not reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the Company; (b) the Seller having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed prior to Closing; and (c) no material adverse effect having occurred with respect to the Company after signing.

6. Indemnification. Following Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for losses arising from breaches of the Seller’s representations, warranties and covenants, subject to customary limitations, including a 12-month survival period for non-fundamental representations, a deductible basket equal to 1% of the Purchase Price, and an aggregate cap equal to 10% of the Purchase Price, except in the case of fraud or willful misconduct.
7. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential.
